scenes.title: FIRST_VALUE()
scenes.narration: FIRST_VALUE returns the first value in the window frame according to the ORDER BY, letting every row reference the leader of its group.

scenes.title: How FIRST_VALUE() Works
bullets: Returns the first row's value in the ordered frame
Order is set by the ORDER BY inside OVER
Every row in the partition sees the same first value
Great for comparing each row to the group leader
scenes.narration: FIRST_VALUE returns the value from the first row in the window frame, as determined by your ORDER BY. Because the default frame starts at the beginning of the partition, every row typically sees the same first value. This makes it easy to compare each row against the leader of its group, such as the top salary or the earliest date.

scenes.title: Top Earner Per Department
scenes.code:
SELECT
  department,
  employee_name,
  salary,
  FIRST_VALUE(employee_name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY department
    ORDER BY salary DESC
  ) AS top_earner
FROM employees;
scenes.narration: This query partitions employees by department and orders them by salary descending, so the highest-paid person sits first in each partition's frame. FIRST_VALUE of employee_name then returns that top earner's name on every row of the department. Now each employee can be compared directly against the leader of their group, all without a self-join or subquery.

scenes.title: How the First Value Is Chosen
steps: Each group is ordered by the ORDER BY clause
The frame starts at the first row of the partition
FIRST_VALUE reads that leading row's value
scenes.narration: The engine partitions the rows, orders each group, and by default sets the frame to begin at the first row of the partition. FIRST_VALUE then simply reads the value from that leading row and returns it. Because the frame's start is fixed, the result is stable across every row in the partition.

scenes.text: FIRST_VALUE() is reliable by default because the frame already starts at the partition's first row — its sibling LAST_VALUE() needs an explicit frame to behave as expected.
scenes.narration: FIRST_VALUE works reliably out of the box because the frame already begins at the first row, unlike LAST_VALUE which needs an explicit frame.
